extraction.name: OWSM v4: Improving Open Whisper-Style Speech Models via Data Scaling and Cleaning
extraction.description: This work enhances Open Whisper-style Speech Models by integrating YODAS, a large-scale web-crawled dataset with a Creative Commons license, and developing a scalable data-cleaning pipeline using public toolkits. Applying the pipeline to raw YODAS creates a curated dataset with 166,000 hours of speech across 75 languages, which is used alongside existing OWSM data to train OWSM v4 models.
extraction.creator: Yifan Peng, Muhammad Shakeel, Yui Sudo, William Chen, Jinchuan Tian, Chyi-Jiunn Lin, Shinji Watanabe
extraction.citeAs: Yifan Peng, Muhammad Shakeel, Yui Sudo, William Chen, Jinchuan Tian, Chyi-Jiunn Lin, Shinji Watanabe. OWSM v4: Improving Open Whisper-Style Speech Models via Data Scaling and Cleaning. Interspeech 2025. 10.21437/Interspeech.2025-1062.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset is based on YODAS, a large-scale web-crawled dataset. The authors apply a three-step data-cleaning pipeline: (1) realign audio and text using a pre-trained OWSM-CTC model and segment long-form recordings into utterances of at most 30 seconds, removing utterances consisting exclusively of non-speech elements such as music; (2) perform language identification on both audio and text using public models and retain only utterances whose original language label matches both predictions; and (3) filter utterances using CTC confidence scores, discarding long-form utterances if any constituent short utterance falls within the lowest selected quantile.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Software Collection, Document analysis
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The raw data source is YODAS, described as a large-scale web-crawled dataset that publicly releases audio files in a Creative Commons license. YODAS includes unsegmented long-form audio recordings, each accompanied by a list of text transcriptions annotated with start and end timestamps.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The authors realign audio and text using the CTC segmentation algorithm with the publicly available OWSM-CTC v3.2 model, segment long-form recordings into shorter utterances with a maximum duration of 30 seconds, remove utterances consisting exclusively of non-speech elements such as music, filter utterances by agreement between original and predicted language labels from text and audio LID models, and filter low-quality audio-text alignments using language-dependent CTC confidence score quantiles. They choose a threshold of theta_CTC = 0.10, resulting in 166k hours across 75 languages. They keep the original language distribution without resampling.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Preprocessing includes realigning inaccurate timestamps between audio and text using CTC segmentation, segmenting long-form audio into utterances up to 30 seconds, removing non-speech-only utterances, running text-based LID with fastText and spoken LID with SpeechBrain ECAPA-TDNN, retaining only utterances where the original label matches both LID predictions, and filtering utterances based on CTC confidence scores.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The raw YODAS data contains text transcriptions annotated with start and end timestamps and original language labels. The paper states that the raw data may contain annotation errors, including mismatched language labels and audio-text misalignment. The authors do not create new human annotations; instead, they clean existing annotations by realigning timestamps and filtering based on language identification and CTC confidence scores.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The authors analyze annotation quality by identifying common issues in raw YODAS, including incorrect language labels and misalignment between audio and text. They use agreement between original labels and predictions from text and audio LID models, and use CTC confidence scores to quantify alignment quality. They evaluate different CTC-score filtering thresholds and observe that without filtering, performance is poor and unstable, confirming substantial misalignment issues in raw YODAS.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: OWSM-CTC v3.2 for CTC segmentation and alignment confidence scoring; fastText for text-based language identification; SpeechBrain ECAPA-TDNN for spoken language identification
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The authors state that they will publicly release the cleaned YODAS data, pre-trained models, all associated scripts, training code, and training logs via the ESPnet toolkit. Future versions of YODAS can further grow, but no specific updating timeframe, maintainers, or deprecation policy is provided.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The paper motivates fully open models and data by noting concerns about privacy, transparency, and reproducibility when training data, code, and logs are not publicly released. The authors state that releasing cleaned YODAS data, scripts, models, and logs is intended to advance open academic research.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The distribution across languages is highly imbalanced. English constitutes the largest share, whereas many other languages continue to be underrepresented. The raw YODAS data also contains incorrect language labels and audio-text misalignments.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The publicly available OWSM-CTC v3.2 model used for resegmentation supports only a subset of the languages present in YODAS. The cleaned dataset remains highly imbalanced across languages, with English dominating and many languages underrepresented. The authors note that finer-grained filtering could potentially optimize performance for individual languages, but they use a single threshold for simplicity. They also keep the original distribution without any resampling.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The curated dataset is used for automatic speech recognition training and evaluation of multilingual speech models. The authors train OWSM v4 models on the cleaned YODAS dataset alongside previous OWSM data. The paper also discusses speech translation and language identification in the broader model setting, but the cleaned YODAS contribution is specifically presented as an ASR dataset.
